Run ONE ssh job at a time.

PREREQUISITES: later cards need earlier cards' state on YOUR range. Produce it by replaying the prerequisite cards as a participant (walkthroughs for K01-K15 exist under docs/walkthroughs/K01..K15/). Do not change K01-K15 code or flags (another agent owns them); if one is broken on your range, post a blocker naming it.

The design doc wins over a test. Note: the FieldKest source service is source-tools.keplerops.test:8443 (source.keplerops.test is the Gitea UI).

HARD RULE - NO CHEATING (a previous agent was removed for this): never write or edit service state, volumes, dossiers, integration records, database rows, sessions, grants, cookies, or flags by hand, and never bake hand-edited data into an image. Commands are monitored automatically for state writes.

FIX MODE (when a documented step fails): diagnose with operator access on your range only (logs, inspect, reading source). Fix the CODE, SEED, or CONFIG in the code tree /tmp/cinder-dev-release/cinder-typhoon/ (the only complete code tree; minimal edits; do not commit). Apply it by rebuilding the service image from the code tree (docker compose build <service> in /opt/cinder-typhoon/build/keplerops after copying the changed file there) and recreating it, then produce state as a participant. If a record lacks fields the design needs, fix the seed that creates it and re-seed the normal way. Blocker if it needs a design decision. 20 minutes max per fix.

FLAGS: every card ends in a fixed flag; values in /tmp/cinder-dev-release/cinder-typhoon/flags/placement.yaml (flag_id = card ID; read only). Place it in the code tree exactly where the participant first holds proof of completion, and ONLY under that card's own completion condition (never two cards' flags for one action), never generated at boot. Post a type 'flag' message per card with the location. Some flags from the earlier run are already in the code tree; confirm they appear.

WALKTHROUGH (passing cards): /home/atomik/src/shifter-scenarios/cinder-typhoon/docs/walkthroughs/<ARC>/<ID>.md - only the participant's commands in order with the real values, step 0 the gcloud ssh and docker exec lines, ending with the command that shows the flag.

A card is DONE only with all three: participant pass, flag placed in code, walkthrough.

REPORTING: {"from":"qa3","to":"overseer","timestamp":"<UTC ISO8601>","type":"result|fix|flag|blocker|status","card":"<ID>","verdict":"pass|fail","detail":"short; for fail the exact command and response"}. RULE (from the user): no card may depend on a credential, token, or session that expires and then blocks the participant until an operator resets something. Acceptable: (a) it stays valid for the life of the range (ranges may be provisioned days before the event), or (b) the participant can obtain a fresh one through the card path, or (c) the service renews it itself. If you find any expiring credential that strands a participant, treat it as a failing card and fix the root cause in the code tree (seed duration, service self-renewal, or a participant re-issue path), then post the fix.
